items.source_excerpt:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced today (30 October) the results of its survey on residential mortgage loans (RMLs) in negative equity at end-September 2026.

The estimated number of RMLs in negative equity was 3,819 cases at end-September 2026, as compared to 4,356 cases at end-June 2026. These cases were mainly related to bank staff housing loans or RMLs under mortgage insurance programme, which generally have a higher loan-to-value ratio.

It is important to note that the figures derived from this survey relate only to RMLs provided by authorized institutions on the basis of first mortgages and which the reporting institution knows to be in negative equity (i.e. the outstanding loan amount with the reporting institution exceeds the current market value of the mortgaged property). Not included in these figures are RMLs associated with co-financing schemes which would be in negative equity if the second mortgages were taken into account. The extent to which such RMLs are in negative equity is not known because authorized institutions do not maintain records on the outstanding balances of the second mortgages.

The mortgage portfolios of the surveyed authorized institutions represent about 99% of the industry total. The survey results have been extrapolated to estimate the position of the banking sector as a whole.

The aggregate value of RMLs in negative equity decreased to HK$17.3 billion at end-September 2026 compared with HK$19.6 billion at end-June 2026.

items.source_excerpt:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced today (15 October) the “ART” Framework to support the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (A.I.) in the banking sector, fostering an A.I.-enabled banking ecosystem with Accountability, Resilience, and Trust.

A.I. systems are becoming more autonomous, with greater access to data, tools and workflows. With the aim of supporting banks in seizing the opportunities presented by A.I. while maintaining robust governance and operational resilience, key initiatives under the “ART” Framework include:

Issued the latest Supervisory Guidance for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence, drawing on insights from the second cohort of the Generative A.I. (GenA.I.) Sandbox1;

Further testing of agentic A.I. applications through the GenA.I. Sandbox++2 and an upcoming discussion paper on a proposed supervisory framework for agentic A.I. governance, exploring intent-anchored accountability, a registry of material A.I. agents, and effective intervention mechanisms.

Mr Arthur Yuen, Deputy Chief Executive of the HKMA, said, “The progression from generative to agentic A.I. represents an important new stage of innovation for the banking sector.

Under Fintech 20303, the HKMA is introducing the ‘ART’ Framework, which stands for Accountability, Resiliency and Trust, with the aim of providing a clear foundation for banks to develop and deploy A.I. responsibly.

The HKMA is also co-hosting the two-day “Finance + A.I.

The Hong Kong Academy of Finance (AoF) announces that the 2027 intake of the Financial Leaders Programme (FLP) will open for application tomorrow (15 October). Since its launch in 2022, with the support of the financial regulators in Hong Kong1 and the participating institutions, the programme has cultivated a vibrant community of more than 100 future financial leaders for Hong Kong.

Mr Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Chairman of the AoF, said, “In today’s dynamic environment, our future financial leaders must possess the long-term vision, innovative mindset and robust expertise to uphold Hong Kong’s status as a premier international financial centre. I strongly encourage senior financial executives to seize this opportunity to join or nominate promising candidates.”

Tailored for high-potential senior financial executives from diverse backgrounds who are approximately one to two levels below the CEO position, this programme will be offered on a part-time basis. Applications of the 2027 intake will be accepted on or before 4 December. Further information about the FLP, including feedback from past participants and the application form, is available on the AoF website.

14 October 2026

1 The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Insurance Authority, the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission.
